info.title: Positron Tanks API
info.description: Programmable robot combat. Errors use one format everywhere: `{"error": {"code", "message", "details"?}}`; branch on `code`. Lists are paged: pass `limit` (1-200, default 50) and, for later pages, the previous response's `nextCursor` as `cursor`, repeating any filters; `nextCursor` is null on the last page.

tags.name: Accounts
tags.description: Signing up, logging in, and API keys.

tags.name: Garage
tags.description: Your private Bot Designs and their immutable Revisions. Programs are visible only to their owner; other Players' designs are indistinguishable from missing ones.

tags.name: Maps
tags.description: Maps and their immutable Revisions. Anyone may read Maps; only a Map's creator may add Revisions, rename or describe it, or archive it.

tags.name: Rulesets
tags.description: The Ruleset versions this server hosts, side by side: each version's rules, language spec, Parts Catalog and Terrain table as data, and the prose documents that explain them as Markdown. Public and frozen per version.

tags.name: Games
tags.description: Creating Games, browsing Open ones, and submitting or withdrawing Entries. A Game starts by itself the moment it is full and is cancelled by itself if not full by its fill deadline. Builds stay hidden while a Game is Open; Programs are never shown.

tags.name: Spectating
tags.description: Watching Games: the latest Tick, a live stream of every Tick, and the Replay once a Game is Finished. Any authenticated Player may watch any Game from Running onward. Programs are never shown; a Bot's Program log goes only to its owner.

post.summary: Create a Bot Design with its first Revision
post.description: Validates the Build (parts exist, Components fit their Slots, cost within the Ruleset's largest Point Budget) and checks the Program; on any problem nothing is saved and every problem is listed in `details`. Program problems have path `program` plus `line` and `column`. The optional `description` and Revision 1's optional `notes` are private to you.

get.summary: List your Bot Designs
get.description: Archived designs are left out unless `includeArchived` is true. Programs are not included.

get.description: Archived designs can still be read.

patch.summary: Rename or describe one of your Bot Designs
patch.description: Changes the name and/or description; fields left out are kept. They belong to the design, not a Revision, so this adds no Revision, and archived designs can be changed too. The description stays private to you.

delete.summary: Archive one of your Bot Designs
delete.description: Deleting a design archives it: it is left out of listings, accepts no new Revisions, and cannot be used in new Entries. It and its Revisions remain readable, since Games may reference them. Archiving an archived design does nothing.

post.summary: Save an edit to one of your Bot Designs as a new Revision
post.description: Validated exactly as when creating a design, under the design's Ruleset version. Earlier Revisions are unchanged. The optional `notes` say what changed (Build and/or Program); like the rest of the Revision they can never be changed, and they are private to you.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: At most this many items.

parameters.name: cursor

parameters.name: revision
parameters.description: The Revision number.

delete.summary: Delete a Revision of one of your Bot Designs that no Game uses
delete.description: Truly deletes the Revision; its number is not reused. Refused with 409 `revision_in_use` if any Game uses it (an Entry in any state, withdrawn Entries aside), and with 409 `latest_revision` for the design's latest Revision, which is its current state (archive the design instead). Revisions of archived designs can be deleted too.

parameters.name: revision
parameters.description: The Revision number.

post.summary: Copy one of your Bot Designs to another Ruleset version
post.description: Re-validates a Revision (the latest by default) under the target Ruleset. If it is valid there, it is saved as a new design in that version, at Revision 1, and the source is untouched. Otherwise nothing is saved and the response is 422 `copy_has_problems` listing every problem (removed Components, a cost over the largest Point Budget, unknown built-ins, ...). With `dryRun` the report is returned with 200 and nothing is saved either way. Archived designs can be copied. The copy keeps the source's description; its Revision 1 takes `notes` from the request (empty if left out), not the source's.

post.summary: Check the tick cost of a Program in a sample world
post.description: Validates the Build and Program exactly as `createBotDesign` does (problems answer 422 with every problem in `details`), then runs the Program's init phase and `tick()` for `ticks` Ticks in the sample world and reports the operations each run used, the peak, and persistent memory. Nothing is saved. A local-server feature: servers that do not enable it answer 410 `feature_disabled` (see `getServerInfo`).

post.summary: Check the tick cost of a Revision of one of your Bot Designs
post.description: As `checkTickCost`, for a saved Revision (the latest by default) under the design's Ruleset version. Archived designs can be checked. Another Player's design answers 404.

post.summary: Create a Map with its first Revision
post.description: Validates the content as Map Format 1 under this server's Map size limits; on any problem nothing is saved and every problem is listed in `details`, with paths such as `map.obstacles[2].hitPoints`. Terrain names are checked against a Ruleset only when a Game uses the Map. The optional `notes` go on Revision 1.

post.description: You become its Initiator; you need not enter it. The Map must not be archived, its Revision must be in a Map Format the Ruleset supports and use only Terrains the Ruleset defines, and `playerCount` may not exceed its Spawn Zones. `pointBudget` must be within the Ruleset's range, and `timeLimitSeconds` and `fillTimeoutSeconds` within the server's maxima. Every problem is listed in `details`.

get.summary: Get a Game with its Entries
get.description: Any Player may read any Game. Other Players' Builds and costs are hidden while the Game is Open (and if it was Cancelled); Programs are never shown.

post.summary: Cancel an Open Game you initiated
Submit an Entry to an Open Game
post.description: Each Bot is one of your unarchived Bot Designs (at a given Revision, the latest by default) authored for the Game's Ruleset, with a Bot Name unique within the Game ignoring case. Together they must cost at most the Point Budget and be few enough for at least one of the Map's Spawn Zones. You may have one Entry in a Game; a second is 422 `validation_failed`. The Entry that fills the Game starts it: it is Running in the response. If the Game is no longer Open (it filled, was cancelled or timed out) the answer is 409 `game_not_open`.

201.description: The new Entry and the Game.

delete.summary: Withdraw one of your Entries from an Open Game
delete.description: The Entry is removed and its slot freed. Once a Game has started, Entries cannot be withdrawn.

get.summary: Get the latest Tick of a Running or Finished Game
get.description: The Game, and its Replay header with only the latest Tick played in `replay.ticks` (the last Tick, once Finished), and what the Ticks before it left behind in `earlier`. Open Games answer 409 `game_not_started`, as do Running Games the server has not started playing yet; Cancelled Games answer 409 `game_cancelled`.

get.summary: Watch a Game live, one event per Tick (Server-Sent Events)
get.description: A `text/event-stream` of JSON events. First a `snapshot` (a GameSnapshot), sent as soon as the Game is being played; then a `tick` (a ReplayTick) for every Tick played after it, in order, with the Tick as the event id; then, once the Game is Finished, an `end` (a GameEnded) and the stream closes. A Finished Game gives its last snapshot and `end` at once. If the stream closes without `end` (the server is restarting, or you read too slowly and fell too far behind), reconnect: you get a fresh snapshot. Comment lines keep idle streams open. Open and Cancelled Games answer 409 as for the snapshot. Browsers must read the stream with `fetch` (a ReadableStream body, sending the bearer `Authorization` header), since the native EventSource cannot send it; on reconnect, send the last event id as `Last-Event-ID`, as EventSource would (the server answers with a fresh snapshot regardless).

200.description: The event stream. Its `data` lines are GameSnapshot (`snapshot`), ReplayTick (`tick`) and GameEnded (`end`) JSON.

get.summary: Get the Replay of a Finished Game
get.description: Every Tick's events and positions, and every participating Build; never a Program. Games not yet Finished answer 409 `game_not_finished`; Cancelled Games, which have no Replay, 409 `game_cancelled`.

get.summary: Get your own Bots' Program logs in a Game
get.description: Runtime errors, halts, operations used and `log()` output of each of your Bots' Program runs, so far while the Game is Running. Only your own Bots are ever included; if you have none in the Game the answer is 404, as it is for a Game Finished before Program logs were kept. Narrow it with `fromTick` and `toTick` (inclusive) to page through a long Game or poll a live one. Open and Cancelled Games answer 409 as for the snapshot.

startedAt.description: When the Game filled and became Running.

endedAt.description: When the Game was Finished or Cancelled.

cancelReason.description: Why a Cancelled Game was cancelled: initiator: its Initiator cancelled it while Open; fill_timeout: it was not full by its fill deadline; server_error: it became Running but the server failed to play it, even after retrying, so it was cancelled unplayed (no result and no Replay).

result.description: Set once the Game is Finished.

nextCursor.description: Pass as `cursor` for the next page; null on the last page.

GameEntryBot.description: One Bot of an Entry. `cost` and `build` are present for your own Entries and, for everyone, once the Game is Running or Finished; `design` only for your own Entries. Programs are never included.

name.description: The Bot Name, unique within the Game.

GameEntry.description: `cost` is present for your own Entries and, for everyone, once the Game is Running or Finished.

cost.description: The combined cost of the Entry's Bots.

mapRevision.description: The Map Revision to play on; defaults to the latest.

playerCount.description: At most the Map Revision's number of Spawn Zones.

pointBudget.description: Within the Ruleset's Point Budget range.

timeLimitSeconds.description: Simulated seconds, at most the server's maximum.

fillTimeoutSeconds.description: Real seconds, at most the server's maximum.

designId.description: One of your unarchived Bot Designs, in the Game's Ruleset.

revision.description: The Revision to enter; defaults to the latest.

name.description: Unique within the Game, ignoring case.

bots.description: Entering one design twice yields two Bots; each needs its own name.

ReplayTick.description: One Tick of a Replay: what happened in it, and where everything was at its end.

tick.description: 0 for the init phase, whose frame shows the starting positions.

events.description: In the order they happened. Each has a `type` (collision, fired, impact, damage, disabled, obstacleDestroyed) and that type's fields, as the Ruleset version's engine spec describes.

bots.description: Every Bot, in Bot id order.

projectiles.description: Projectiles in flight, in id order.

Replay.description: A Game's full history of events plus every participating Build, never a Program. The shape is the Ruleset version's; this describes r1.

bots.description: In Bot id order; Bot ids are numbered from 1 across all Entries.

ticks.description: Every Tick, from the init phase (Tick 0).

result.description: How the Game ended, with Players by id; null while it is Running.

winner.description: The winning Player's id; null for a Draw.

standings.description: One per Player, in order of their first Entry.

EarlierTicks.description: What the Ticks before a snapshot's Tick left behind, so a Spectator joining then sees the Game as it stands. Its size depends on the Map and the Bots, not on how long the Game has run. The shape is the Ruleset version's; this describes r1.

beforeTick.description: The Ticks summarized are those before this one: the snapshot's Tick.

obstaclesDestroyed.description: Every `obstacleDestroyed` event of those Ticks, in order.

disabled.description: Every `disabled` event of those Ticks, in order.

damage.description: Hit Points removed from Bots (`damage` events' `dealt`) in those Ticks, summed per dealer and target, in the order each pair first took damage. A shot is dealt by the Bot that fired it, a ram by the other Bot; a ram into a wreck, an Obstacle or the boundary by no Bot (`dealer` null).

GameSnapshot.description: A Game and its Replay so far, with only the latest Tick in `replay.ticks`, and what the Ticks before it left behind in `earlier`.

GameEnded.description: The `end` event's data: the Game, now Finished, with its result.

bots.description: Your Bots in the Game, in Bot id order.

bot.description: The Bot's id in the Replay.

runs.description: Every run of the Program in the Ticks asked for, in Tick order; Tick 0 is the init phase.

error.description: Where and why the run stopped early, or null.

memoryCells.description: Persistent state at the end of the run, in cells.

halt.description: Why the Program halted after this run, or null.

logTruncated.description: Whether `log()` output was dropped for this run.

Error.description: An error, in the shared error format.

bearerAuth.description: A session token (from `logIn`) or an API key (from `createApiKey`).
